title: The Voice Is Heard
summary: A voice is heard throughout the earth, warning the people to repent and lamenting the slain sons and daughters.

explicit_facts.text: A voice is heard among all the inhabitants of the earth, across the face of the land.
The voice warns the people to repent and says the devil and his angels rejoice over the slain sons and daughters.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The voice can be represented as unseen, with listeners suggested across the land.
unspecified_visual_details: The voice’s source, sound appearance, and the listeners’ individual identities are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wo, wo, wo unto this people;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

narration.text: there was a voice heard among all the inhabitants of the earth,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The voice’s words continue as a proclamation in subsequent scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the devil or angels as visible participants; their rejoicing is reported, not shown as a present event.

title: Zarahemla Burned
summary: The voice says that Zarahemla and its inhabitants were burned with fire.

explicit_facts.text: The voice says it burned Zarahemla and its inhabitants with fire.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The city may be shown burning as an illustration of the reported destruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the city, its inhabitants, and the circumstances of the burning are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: that great city Zarahemla have I burned with fire,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction is reported by the voice; it is not a newly occurring event in the present setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent individual inhabitants, actions, or details of the fire.

title: Moroni Sunk
summary: The voice says that Moroni was sunk into the sea and its inhabitants drowned.

explicit_facts.text: The voice says Moroni was caused to sink into the depths of the sea and its inhabitants drowned.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The city may be represented beneath the sea to illustrate the reported destruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The city’s appearance and the manner in which it sank are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: that great city Moroni have I caused to be sunk
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction is reported rather than staged as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict drowning individuals or invent details of the sinking.

title: Moronihah Covered
summary: The voice says that Moronihah and its inhabitants were covered with earth.

explicit_facts.text: The voice says Moronihah and its inhabitants were covered with earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Earth covering the city can illustrate the reported destruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The city’s appearance and the manner of covering are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: that great city Moronihah have I covered with earth,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The voice explains that this hides iniquities and abominations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show identifiable inhabitants or add details of the event.

title: Gilgal Sunk
summary: The voice says that Gilgal and its inhabitants were sunk and buried in the depths of the earth.

explicit_facts.text: The voice says Gilgal was caused to sink and its inhabitants were buried in the depths of the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A sunken city may illustrate the reported destruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The city’s appearance and the manner of sinking are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: the city of Gilgal have I caused to be sunk,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction is recounted by the voice.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show individual inhabitants or invent details of the sinking.

title: Cities Replaced by Waters
summary: The voice names Onihah, Mocum, and Jerusalem, saying their inhabitants were destroyed and waters came up in their place.

explicit_facts.text: The voice names the cities of Onihah, Mocum, and Jerusalem and their inhabitants.
The voice says waters came up in their place.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The three cities may be shown as separate inset illustrations of water occupying their places.
unspecified_visual_details: The cities’ appearances and the sequence or manner of destruction are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: and waters have I caused to come up in the stead thereof,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse names three cities in one summarized report; it does not specify separate moments.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a sequence of destruction or show named cities as a single geographic location.

title: Four Cities Sunk
summary: The voice says Gadiandi, Gadiomnah, Jacob, and Gimgimno were sunk, leaving hills and valleys where they had been.

explicit_facts.text: The voice says the four named cities were sunk, hills and valleys made in their places, and their inhabitants buried in the depths of the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Separate small views may illustrate the named cities and the altered terrain in their places.
unspecified_visual_details: The cities’ appearances and the exact geography of the hills and valleys are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: all these have I caused to be sunk,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports multiple city destructions without specifying their order.
prohibited_inventions: Do not combine the cities into one location or invent a chronological sequence.

title: Jacobugath Burned
summary: The voice says Jacobugath and its inhabitants were burned because of their sins and wickedness.

explicit_facts.text: Jacobugath was inhabited by the people of king Jacob.
The voice says it caused Jacobugath to be burned with fire because of sins, wickedness, secret murders, and combinations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The city may be illustrated burning as a report of its destruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The people of king Jacob are not individually identified; the city’s appearance and the event’s particulars are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: that great city Jacobugath,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

narration.text: have I caused to be burned with fire

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Secret murders and combinations are cited as the reason for the city’s destruction.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a secret murder, a conspiracy, or named individuals; these are reported causes, not shown events.

title: Four Cities Burned
summary: The voice says Laman, Josh, Gad, and Kishkumen were burned with their inhabitants because they cast out prophets and stoned those sent to them.

explicit_facts.text: The voice says the four named cities and their inhabitants were burned with fire.
The voice says the people cast out prophets and stoned those sent to declare their wickedness, and that fire was sent down to destroy them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The cities may be represented in separate small views; the burning is a reported event.
unspecified_visual_details: The prophets’ identities, the cities’ appearances, and the timing of these events are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: I did send down fire and destroy them,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The voice connects the destruction with the people’s rejection of prophets.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier stoning or portray fire striking people in graphic detail.

title: Many Destructions
summary: The voice says many great destructions came upon the land and its people because of wickedness and abominations.

explicit_facts.text: The voice says many great destructions came upon the land and its people because of wickedness and abominations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A restrained overview of altered land may suggest the reported destructions.
unspecified_visual_details: The locations and appearances of the additional destructions are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: many great destructions have I caused to come upon this land,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a summary statement, not a newly specified destruction event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent additional named cities or particular disasters.

title: Call to Repentance
summary: The voice calls those spared to return, repent, be converted, and come to Christ, promising healing and eternal life.

explicit_facts.text: The voice addresses those spared because they were more righteous than those destroyed, urging them to return, repent, and be converted.
The voice promises eternal life to those who come and says it will receive them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The voice may be represented off-screen while the spared are present as listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity, number, appearance, and setting of those spared are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: will ye not now return unto me,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

spoken_dialogue.text: whosoever will come, him will I receive;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The address is a teaching and invitation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show healing as a performed miracle; it is promised.

title: Jesus Christ Identifies Himself
summary: The speaker identifies himself as Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and speaks of creation, his relationship with the Father, and his rejected coming.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker identifies himself as Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and says he created the heavens and the earth and was with the Father from the beginning.
The speaker says he came to his own, was not received, and that scriptures concerning his coming are fulfilled.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker remains off-screen; the passage does not describe a visible appearance.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s physical appearance and the listeners’ setting are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: I am Jesus Christ the Son of God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

spoken_dialogue.text: I came unto my own,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The speaker’s claims are delivered as speech, not illustrated as separate creation or rejection scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not visibly depict Jesus Christ; his appearance is not described here.

title: Redemption and Fulfillment
summary: The speaker promises believers becoming children of God and declares redemption through him, fulfillment of the law of Moses, and that he is the light and life of the world.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says those who receive him may become children of God, that redemption comes through him, and that the law of Moses is fulfilled in him.
The speaker says he is the light and life of the world, Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be represented with the speaker off-screen.
unspecified_visual_details: No visual appearance of the speaker or literal light effect is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: by me redemption cometh,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

spoken_dialogue.text: I am the light and the life of the world.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Light,” “life,” “Alpha,” and “Omega” are expressed as teachings, not narrated visual events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict metaphors as literal supernatural scenes.

title: A New Offering
summary: The speaker says blood offerings and burnt offerings are no longer accepted, calling instead for a broken heart and contrite spirit.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says blood sacrifices and burnt offerings are done away and will not be accepted.
The speaker calls for a broken heart and contrite spirit, and promises to baptize those who come with them with fire and the Holy Ghost.
The speaker cites the Lamanites’ faith and conversion, saying they were baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost and knew it not.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be shown as off-screen speech without depicting a ritual or supernatural baptism.
unspecified_visual_details: The listeners and any physical setting or appearance of baptism are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: And ye shall offer for a sacrifice unto me a broken heart
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

spoken_dialogue.text: and a contrite spirit.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lamanites’ conversion is referred to retrospectively, not presented as a current scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show blood sacrifice, fire baptism, the Holy Ghost’s appearance, or the Lamanites’ earlier conversion as present events.

title: Come as a Little Child
summary: The speaker says he came to bring redemption and save the world from sin, and invites all to repent and come as a little child to be received and saved.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says he came to bring redemption and save the world from sin.
The speaker promises to receive those who repent and come as a little child, and invites the ends of the earth to come and be saved.
The speaker says he laid down his life and took it up again.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be represented with the speaker off-screen.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s appearance, listeners, setting, and details of the referenced death and rising are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: whoso repenteth and cometh unto me as a little child,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

spoken_dialogue.text: repent, and come unto me ye ends of the earth,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The voice

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The laying down and taking up of life are spoken of retrospectively; no separate event is shown.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the crucifixion, resurrection, or a visible appearance of Jesus Christ.
